notes:
{五百|ごひゃく} is ⟦{五|ご}→五：00697_go⟧ (five) + ⟦{百|ひゃく}→百：00780_hyaku⟧ (hundred). No sound change occurs — ひゃく stays as ひゃく after ご.

SOUND CHANGES IN HUNDREDS:
The hundreds have irregular pronunciation for certain numbers:
- {三百|さんびゃく}: rendaku (ひゃく → びゃく)
- ⟦{六百|ろっぴゃく}→六百：30450_roppyaku⟧: sokuon + h→p (ひゃく → ぴゃく)
- ⟦{八百|はっぴゃく}→八百：30452_happyaku⟧: sokuon + h→p
- {五百|ごひゃく}: no change

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {五百|ごひゃく}{円|えん}{玉|だま}: 500-yen coin (the highest-value coin in Japan)
- {五百|ごひゃく}⟦{人|にん}→〜人：00658_nin⟧: 500 people
- {五百|ごひゃく}⟦メートル→メートル：02975_meetoru⟧: 500 meters

CULTURAL NOTE:
The {五百|ごひゃく}{円|えん}{玉|だま} is notable as the largest-denomination coin in regular circulation in Japan. It is commonly saved in ⟦{貯金箱|ちょきんばこ}→貯金箱：15345_chokinbako⟧ (piggy banks) as a form of casual savings known as {五百|ごひゃく}{円|えん}{玉|だま}⟦{貯金|ちょきん}→貯金：03497_chokin⟧.
